title: Extremely rare white African wild dog puppy 4 Rivers is currently home to an extraordinary pack of wild dogs with a very leucistic pup. Local researchers have confirmed that this is extremely rare and virtually unheard of in Botswana for the past 30 years or so 🐾 In the 1990s, guides first spotted leucistic puppies in the Kwando area. The males of Kwando's pack have dispersed. These men, identified by photos, established a group dubbed the Golden Pack in the Vumbura area. Some descendants of this golden pack started another family in Kwara, where leucism was still evident but somewhat diluted. Leucism tends to be a lack of melanin in the skin, feathers, or hair. Melanin is the natural pigment responsible for most brown and black coloring. It is mostly genetic and varies in degree, going all the way to pure white in rare cases (like this one at 4 Rivers) or like in the "golden" Vumbura dogs, which are a pale tan tone. Currently, the pup interacts normally with its siblings and adult painted wolves (as African wild dogs are also known). Although this little one is anything but painted! If anything, it's dominant in the hierarchy when it comes to receiving food from adults! This pup may darken as he ages, and there is an outward chance that his whole body will be a large white spot, which sometimes happens with domestic dogs and cats. We'll keep a close eye to see how its color evolves 🐶 Thanks to the expert researchers in Botswana for their insight! Dr Peter Apps Dr John Tico McNutt Dr Gabriele Cozzi Botswana Predator Conservation

title: The Kampala Flyover Road Project is a road-improvement initiative in the Central Division of Kampala, the capital city of Uganda. Here are the key details: Objective: The project aims to decongest the city by separating through-traffic from city-street traffic. It focuses on traffic entering the city, mainly from Entebbe along the old Kampala-Entebbe Road and from Mpigi along the Kampala-Mpigi Expressway. Construction: The project involves constructing flyovers at the “Clock Tower” and “Kitgum House,” widening Nsambya Road and Mukwano Road, and improving interfacing roads and junctions. The project stretches over approximately 3.5 kilometers (2 miles). Funding: The Ugandan government, with financing from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), funds the project. Progress: Despite challenges posed by the COVID-19 outbreak, construction is progressing steadily. Excavation works on the 4-lane underpass are nearing completion, and screw piles for the flyover and pedestrian bridges have been delivered on-site12. title: Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez paid tribute to the late #Pose Actress Cecilia Gentili. Cecilia Gentili, an Argentina-born artist and activist known for her work in the immigrant and transgender rights movements in New York City, is being widely remembered following her death last week. She was 52. As an actress, Gentili stood out with her memorable portrayal of Ms. Orlando on the groundbreaking series Pose, which illuminated the experiences of trans women of colour during the AIDS crisis of the 1980s. News of her death broke on Tuesday (February 6), when close friends and family took to her Instagram page to announce her passing, saying: “Our beloved Cecilia Gentili passed away this morning to continue watching over us in spirit. Please be gentle with each other and love one another with ferocity.” Gentili was seen by many as a symbol of hope and resilience. Her journey from Argentina to the bustling streets of New York City was marked by her continuing unwavering advocacy for marginalised communities, from undocumented immigrants to sex workers. She took pivotal roles at prominent organisations like New York City–based AIDS non-profit GMHC and founded Trans Equity Consulting, where her mission was to amplify the voices of marginalised communities. Her activism also took the form of initiatives like Transmissions Fest, a music festival aimed at putting transgender voices centre stage, and fundraising event Fierce Futures in support of Black trans people. Tributes to Cecilia poured in across social media from a range of people from all walks of life. American writer and book editor Raquel Willis said: “Cecilia Gentili was a living legend. A titan, an unapologetic example of trans joy and power. Her spirit lives on in all whom she touched and all she built for us. Rest powerfully and peacefully, Mami. And go kiki with the ancestors. You deserve eternal pleasure.” All of the tributes made one thing very clear: that Cecilia Gentili’s impact had transcended boundaries and will linger for decades to come. #ceciliagentili #trans #lgbt #aoc #uspolitics

title: Galápagos penguins are endangered, with an estimate of fewer than 2,000 individuals remaining. A new study using model predictions has uncovered a likely rapid accumulation of microplastics across the food web, with the most microplastics building up in the endangered penguins, then moving down the food web to barracuda, anchovies, sardines, herrings, black-striped salema, and zooplankton. “The goal of this food web bioaccumulation modeling work was to provide science and data to support risk management of hazardous plastic waste, reduce microplastic emissions in the oceans and marine remote UNESCO Heritage sites such as the Galápagos Islands, and inform local and international marine policy to conserve endangered, endemic seabird species of Galápagos Marine Reserve,” Juan Jose Alava, senior author of the study and principal investigator of the Ocean Pollution Research Unit at the University of British Columbia’s Institute for the Oceans and Fisheries Full article below https://www.ecowatch.com/microplastics-galapagos-penguins.html

The study mentioned predicts rapid microplastic build-up among various marine species, including barracuda, anchovies, sardines, herrings, black-striped salema, and zooplankton. The goal of this research is to support risk management for hazardous plastic waste, reduce microplastic emissions in oceanic areas like the Galápagos Islands, and inform policies to protect endangered seabirds.
